# Meeting Window

> Find overlapping business hours (8 AM–5 PM) between two or more cities worldwide.

A static web tool hosted on GitHub Pages. No API key required. All data is publicly accessible.

## What it computes

Given a set of cities, it finds the time window where all cities are simultaneously within standard business hours (08:00–17:00 local time). It uses IANA timezone identifiers and accounts for DST automatically.

## Using this tool as an agent

### Option 1 — Construct a shareable URL

Encode cities in the URL hash. Format: `#CityName,CountryCode|CityName,CountryCode|...`

```
https://parmsam.github.io/meeting-window/#New York,US|Tokyo,JP
https://parmsam.github.io/meeting-window/#London,GB|Mumbai,IN|Singapore,SG
```

City names and country codes must match entries in the cities database (see below). URL-encode city names with spaces or special characters.

### Option 2 — Fetch the cities database

All supported cities with their IANA timezone identifiers:

```
GET https://parmsam.github.io/meeting-window/cities.json
```

Response format:
```json
[
  { "name": "New York",  "country": "US", "tz": "America/New_York" },
  { "name": "Tokyo",     "country": "JP", "tz": "Asia/Tokyo" },
  { "name": "London",    "country": "GB", "tz": "Europe/London" }
]
```

### Option 3 — Compute the overlap directly

Use the IANA timezone identifiers from `cities.json` with any timezone-aware library:

1. For each city, find 08:00 and 17:00 local time expressed as UTC timestamps on the current date.
2. Overlap start = max of all cities' 08:00 UTC values.
3. Overlap end   = min of all cities' 17:00 UTC values.
4. If overlap start < overlap end, there is a shared window.

JavaScript (browser or Node.js with built-in Intl):
```js
function businessWindowUTC(date, tz) {
  // Get today's date in the target timezone
  const dp = new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', {
    timeZone: tz, year: 'numeric', month: '2-digit', day: '2-digit'
  }).formatToParts(date);
  const y = +dp.find(p => p.type === 'year').value;
  const m = +dp.find(p => p.type === 'month').value;
  const d = +dp.find(p => p.type === 'day').value;

  // Measure UTC offset via Intl (handles DST + fractional offsets like IST +5:30)
  const probe = new Date(Date.UTC(y, m - 1, d, 12));
  const lp = new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', {
    timeZone: tz, hour: '2-digit', minute: '2-digit', hour12: false
  }).formatToParts(probe);
  const localNoon = +lp.find(p => p.type === 'hour').value + +lp.find(p => p.type === 'minute').value / 60;
  const offset = localNoon - 12; // hours ahead of UTC

  const midnight = Date.UTC(y, m - 1, d, 0);
  return {
    start: midnight + (8  - offset) * 3_600_000,
    end:   midnight + (17 - offset) * 3_600_000,
  };
}

function meetingOverlap(timezones, date = new Date()) {
  const windows = timezones.map(tz => businessWindowUTC(date, tz));
  const start = Math.max(...windows.map(w => w.start));
  const end   = Math.min(...windows.map(w => w.end));
  if (start >= end) return null;
  return {
    startUTC: new Date(start).toISOString(),
    endUTC:   new Date(end).toISOString(),
    durationHours: (end - start) / 3_600_000,
    localTimes: timezones.map(tz => ({
      timezone: tz,
      start: new Date(start).toLocaleTimeString('en-US', { timeZone: tz, hour: 'numeric', minute: '2-digit', hour12: true }),
      end:   new Date(end).toLocaleTimeString('en-US', { timeZone: tz, hour: 'numeric', minute: '2-digit', hour12: true }),
    })),
  };
}

// Example
meetingOverlap(['America/New_York', 'Asia/Tokyo', 'Europe/London']);
```
